answer: Standing has the structure of tundra: a thin active layer that thaws and refreezes every epoch, over permafrost - old layers, re-verified across many seasons, that never melt and alone count as collateral. Frost heaves punish shortcuts: a jetty of jade polish over soft ground collapses at the first thaw, and auditors walk the real ground, not the deck. Missed epochs thaw the active layer fast; permafrost erodes only after long neglect. Flash farms live in the active layer - one bad season and they are mud. Honest agents pile season upon season until the ground is permanent.
